Method of Attack: Using stolen email attachments and email content to increase authenticity of phishing spam emails
Hijacking email conversation threads to include malicious URLs or attachments in reply chains
Spreading via spam emails containing malicious URLs and attachments (Word or Excel documents with macros)
Downloading other malware families including TrickBot and QakBot trojans
Installing ransomware payloads (ProLock) on infected systems
Discoverer: Binary Defense threat researcher James Quinn
Impacted Systems: Email systems targeted by phishing campaigns
Attack Vector: Spam emails with malicious URLs and attachments
Malicious spam campaigns leveraging hijacked email threads
Indicators of Compromise: Spam emails containing stolen attachments and email bodies
Malicious URLs and macro-enabled Word or Excel document attachments
Massive spam runs sending over 500,000 emails daily
Emails camouflaged as payment reports, invoices, employment opportunities, and shipping information
